bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Agri dept to provide free sugarcane seeds to farmers under expansion scheme
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Muzaffarpur: The Bihar Agriculture Department will provide free sugarcane seed to farmers to encourage expansion of sugarcane cultivation across the state. Under the Sugarcane Expansion Scheme, farmers will be supported for cultivation across 200 acres, with applications to be submitted online, Jagran reported. Farmers cultivating up to one hectare will be eligible to receive the seed free of cost. The initiative is aimed at increasing the area under sugarcane cultivation and improving farm incomes. Assistant Sugarcane Director Arvind Kumar Ravi said a special campaign would be conducted across all 16 blocks of Muzaffarpur district to promote sugarcane planting. Farmers from each block can apply online to avail themselves of the scheme. The government will also provide subsidies to farmers for purchasing fertilizers and pesticides as part of the initiative. The department plans to promote sugarcane cultivation through greater access to quality planting material and cultivation support. Ravi said farmers could adopt two methods of sugarcane cultivation. In the first method, cane stalks are cut and planted directly in the field, requiring around 25 quintals of seed per acre. The second method involves planting nursery-raised seedlings, with around 10,000 plants required per acre. Sugarcane planting is generally undertaken in October and February. Once the crop is established from the initial planting material, farmers can obtain two additional crops through ratooning with the application of fertilizers and other inputs, according to the department. Under the scheme, farmers will be able to obtain planting material from designated nurseries. The department will directly pay the cost of the seed to the nursery operators. Ravi said sugarcane cultivation could provide significant returns to farmers. According to the department, an acre can produce around 300–400 quintals of sugarcane, potentially generating a profit of around ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh after cultivation costs. The department said it would continue implementing schemes to promote sugarcane cultivation and support higher farm incomes in Bihar.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments - Saur Energy
bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet. Manish Kumar 18 Sep 2026 09:48 IST Follow Us Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments Photograph: (AI) The Bihar Horticulture Development Society has invited bids from OEMs and authorised agencies for the supply, installation and maintenance of solar crop dryers across multiple capacity categories, ranging from 20 kg to 1,000 kg per batch. Advertisment The Bihar Horticulture Development Society (BHDS), under the state’s Department of Agriculture, has floated a request for proposal (RFP) to empanel Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and OEM-authorised agencies for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, warranty support and maintenance of solar crop dryers across Bihar. Advertisment The procurement covers solar crop dryers with capacities of 20/25 kg, 50 kg, 100 kg, 250 kg, 500 kg and a special 1,000-kg category, according to the RFP. The dryers are intended to support farmers and horticulture-related users in drying agricultural and horticultural produce. The tender has been floated through the Bihar government's e-procurement portal. The last date for submission of bids is October 8, 2026, at 3 pm, while technical bids are scheduled to open the same day at 3:30 pm. A pre-bid meeting is scheduled for September 24 at 1:15 pm in hybrid/online mode. The date for financial bid opening will be communicated to technically qualified bidders. Advertisment Six capacity categories The RFP has divided the solar crop dryers into different capacity packages based on their intended users. The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet, box or foldable configurations envisaged. The 50-kg category is intended for progressive farmers, small self-help groups (SHGs), nurseries and demonstration centres, while the 100-kg category targets SHGs, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), village enterprises and common facility centres. Advertisment The larger 250-kg package is designed for FPOs, farmer clusters and institutional buyers, while the 500-kg category targets large FPOs, aggregation centres and processing clusters. A special 1,000-kg category is reserved for cluster or institutional projects and can be deployed only after site feasibility, civil-space confirmation, power/backup planning and separate approval by BHDS. Advertisment Solar-powered drying system The tender defines a solar crop dryer as a protected drying system using solar thermal energy and/or solar PV-powered air circulation/control, with an optional hybrid backup, for controlled drying of agricultural and horticultural produce. The minimum technical specifications require an indirect solar crop dryer with forced convection. The systems are expected to handle fruits, vegetables, spices, medicinal and aromatic plants, grains and other agricultural or horticultural products. The dryers will have to use SS 304 food-grade trays and food-contact surfaces, while the drying temperature range is specified at 40°C to 70°C. Air circulation is to be achieved through solar-powered DC fans or blowers, with protection against bird and animal intrusion. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry. Inaugurating SEMICON India 2026 at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said the world is looking for new and trusted manufacturing destinations and India is steadily preparing itself to meet this need. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth.. He discussed how the explosive demand for Artificial Intelligence is shifting the focus from mere transistor size to holistic system integration, including memory placement and heat management. Mr Modi said that on one side India’s economy is growing and the other side, global trust in India is also growing. He said, despite the challenging global environment, India recorded a growth rate of 7.8 per cent. Prime Minister said, at the same time, Japan’s credit rating agency also upgraded India’s sovereign rating. Mr Modi said, every citizen of the country is working with a commitment to build a developed India. Prime Minister said, India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and it is is opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth. Prime Minister Modi said, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 expanded outlay to 13.5 billion US dollar from eight billion US dollar in the first phase. He highlighted that so far 12 chip making projects have been approved in the next phase it will further increase. In his address, the Prime Minister also mentioned about recently held BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He said, India successfully hosted the summit in which New Delhi Declaration was adopted with consensus of every member country. Mr Modi said, it is another major testament to the world’s trust in India. He said, young talents who are researching in India should come forward. Mr Modi said, the youth who are researching abroad should also join the development of advanced technologies in India. He urged industry leaders to spearhead Research and Development in the country. He added that this will be mutually beneficial, driving industry growth while empowering India’s youth. On the occasion, Union Minister of Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw said that India had wanted to establish a semiconductor industry for several decades, but it was possible only under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the foundation has now been laid and the next step is to build the industry through Semicon 2.0, which focuses on six major pillars. This include semiconductor design, machines and materials, memory, silicon, compound and logic fabrication units and research and development. He said, the government has set a target to support at least 200 startups and companies to design chips in India across the spectrum of semiconductor requirements. Minister of State for Electronics and IT Jitin Prasada, Secretary S Krishnan, officials, delegations were present on the occasion. The SEMICON India 2026 event has brought together over 600 exhibitors, 300 international companies, and delegations from more than 50 countries. The exhibition features six country pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, twelve State Government pavilions, and a dedicated Startup Pavilion.The conference and exhibition, being held from today is being organised on the theme Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem. It has brought together global and Indian companies, policymakers, investors, researchers, start-ups, academic institutions and students from across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

national_raw_news.content: PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 06:18 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) celebrated the 3rd Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal, on Thursday. According to a release from the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, the occasion marked three years of the Scheme’s implementation and highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen the livelihoods, skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of traditional artisans and craftspeople. West Bengal onboarded for the implementation of PM Vishwakarma in May, marking an important step towards extending comprehensive support to the State’s traditional artisans and craftspeople. The celebrations in Kolkata underscored the scheme’s significance in empowering Vishwakarmas through skill training, modern tools, institutional credit and market linkages. On the occasion of the 3rd Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma, an exhibition showcasing the rich traditional arts and crafts of Vishwakarma artisans was inaugurated by Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Cabinet Minister, Ministry of MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal and Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal. The exhibition provided Vishwakarmas of West Bengal, a platform to showcase their traditional craftsmanship and entrepreneurial skills. Addressing the gathering, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the importance of extending skill training and credit support to traditional artisans and craftspeople in the state. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the transformative vision behind PM Vishwakarma and acknowledged its significant role in strengthening the livelihood of artisans and craftspeople across the country. Outlining the progress of PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal, he stated that more than 7 lakh applications have been received under the scheme. He stated that the Government of West Bengal will expedite the provision of facilitative support to enable Vishwakarmas to avail the benefits under the scheme. The Chief Minister also assured coordinated efforts by the State for effective and timely implementation of PM Vishwakarma across West Bengal in association with the Ministry of MSME, Government of India. He called upon the concerned State agencies to strengthen outreach and implementation so that the benefits of the scheme reach every eligible artisan and craftsperson. He appreciated the implementation of various schemes and initiatives of the Ministry of MSME in West Bengal, noting their contribution to promoting entrepreneurship, generating employment, supporting enterprise development and strengthening the MSME ecosystem in the State. He emphasised that effective implementation of these initiatives would contribute towards realising PM Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat. national_raw_news.title: HAL to hand over Tejas Trainers, HTT-40s & Dhruv NG Helicopters to IAF - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: HAL to hand over Tejas Trainers, HTT-40s & Dhruv NG Helicopters to IAF; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to attend Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर HAL to hand over Tejas Trainers, HTT-40s & Dhruv NG Helicopters to IAF; Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to attend ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 06:23 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) will hand over Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas Final Operational Clearance (FOC) Twin Seater Trainers & HTT 40 Basic Trainer Aircraft to the Indian Air Force (IAF) and Dhruv Next Generation (NG) helicopters to Pawan Hans Limited (PHL) in the presence of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu in Bengaluru, Karnataka, on Friday. According to a release from the Ministry of Defence, the handover marks an important milestone in the country’s self-reliance journey, as the event would highlight the role being played by HAL and its industry partners in strengthening the domestic aerospace ecosystem. It would also demonstrate the industry’s expanding capability to design, develop, and manufacture advanced platforms for both civil & military applications. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh; Secretary (Defence Production) Sanjeev Kumar; Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation Samir Kumar Sinha; CMD, HAL Ravi K, and other senior officials of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Civil Aviation, IAF, PHL, regulatory agencies and stakeholders from the aerospace & defence sectors will be present on the occasion. The Government has accorded high priority to promoting indigenous design, development and manufacturing in the aerospace & defence sectors. The induction of these platforms is another step towards strengthening the indigenous capabilities and reducing dependence on foreign sources. Earlier on Thursday, Rajnath Singh, along with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and Union Food Processing Industries Minister Chirag Paswan, flagged off a bike yatra from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency, Varanasi, to his birthplace, Vadnagar, in Gujarat, as part of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' on his 76th birthday. The event was organised at the Rudraksh International Cooperation and Conference Centre in Sigra. The yatra will cover the journey from Modi's 'Karmabhoomi' Varanasi to his birthplace, Vadnagar, with 500 people participating on 250 bikes. The Chief Guest of the programme flagged off the bike yatra from Varanasi to his birthplace, Vadnagar, organised at Rudraksh International Cooperation and Conference Centre, Sigra, on Thursday. The programme was started by lighting the lamp by Naidu, Union Food Processing Minister Chirag Paswan, and garlanding the statues of Shyama Prasad Mukherjee and Pt. Deendayal Upadhyay. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Culture Ministry of Culture organises ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme at Purana Qila on the birthday of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Under the leadership of the Prime Minister, public trust has been strengthened in the country and efforts have been made to take development forward with public participation: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Posted On: 18 SEP 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi On the occasion of the birthday of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Ministry of Culture organised the ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme at Purana Qila, New Delhi, on 17th September 2026. Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated the programme by lighting the Aashirwad Ka Diya, organised under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan with the chant of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”. In his address, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that the Aashirwad Ka Diya is not just a lamp, but a symbol of the power of people's blessings, service, gratitude and the resolve for a Viksit Bharat. He said that in Indian culture, the diya gives the message of burning itself to spread light in others' lives, dispelling darkness and paving the way for public welfare. In this spirit, this lamp is also a symbol of collective resolve towards service to the nation. Wishing the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday, the Union Minister said that his public life has been dedicated to national interest and public service. He said that from his childhood till today, in whatever role he has got an opportunity to work, he has worked with full dedication and a spirit of service, keeping the nation supreme. From taking charge as the Chief Minister of Gujarat to leading the country as the Prime Minister, his commitment to national service, public welfare and development has remained constant, he added. Sharing his experience of working with the Prime Minister, Shri Shekhawat said that getting the opportunity to work with the Prime Minister has been an honourable experience of his public life. He said that he has seen Shri Narendra Modi not only as a Prime Minister, but as a dedicated worker, seeker, ascetic and organizer. He said that the Prime Minister inspires people at every level through his conduct, working style and guidance and considers public office not as prestige, but as a medium of responsibility and service. The Union Minister said that the Prime Minister's working style is based on outcome-oriented governance. Schemes are reviewed not just on the basis of processes or data, but on the basis of their actual impact on society and the change reaching the last person, he said. Union Minister added that the Prime Minister's clear view is that merely moving a file forward is not the completion of work, but the public-welfare results arising from it is the real yardstick of good governance. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Education Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi launches the six-month Certificate (Bridge) Course in Primary Teacher Education The Course will provide comprehensive training to in-service primary school teachers to promote quality education Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi launched the six-month Certificate (Bridge) Course in Primary Teacher Education (PTE) on Sept 16, 2026 in New Delhi. The Course is tailored for in-service primary school teachers who hold a B.Ed. degree. It will serve as a critical pathway for such teachers to attain certification to teach at the primary level. This specialized professional development programme will provide comprehensive training to help teachers to develop the necessary skills and competencies to effectively educate learners at the primary level (I-V). The Bridge Course will be implemented through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) and will equip teachers with child-centred, inclusive and development-appropriate teaching practices, strengthening the quality of education at the foundational and primary stages. Designed as per the framework of National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), the Course will strengthen primary-stage pedagogical competencies through academic learning, at least 10 days of online contact classes and at least 20 days of school-based experience. The Course will enable teachers to cater to the diverse learning needs of young children. Comprising six theory courses and a school-based practicum, the programme provides a robust framework to connect educational theory with classroom practice. The Bridge Course aims at empowering primary teachers with the skills, attitudes and reflective capacities necessary to ensure quality education and lifelong learning for all children in primary classrooms. It promotes a vision of teaching as a dynamic, context-sensitive, and inquiry-based profession. The Supreme Court of India vide judgement dated 08.04.2024 in Civil Appeal No. 5068 of 2023 titled Devesh Sharma Vs. Union of India and Ors., had empowered NCTE to devise a bridge course for those appointees who were appointed as primary teachers but did not have D.El.Ed qualification. Accordingly, the Bridge Course was designed for in-service primary school teachers appointed between 28 June 2018 to 11 August 2023 to teach at the primary level (Classes I-V) with a B.Ed. degree. This course is specifically intended for those teachers whose appointments are protected under the NCTE Gazette Notification F. No. NCTE-Reg. 012/2018 dated 28th June 2018. The programme includes both theoretical and practical components aimed at foundational learning principles. The medium of the instruction shall be Hindi and English languages. However, the teachers will be allowed to write the Public Examination (Theory) in any of the 22 scheduled languages listed in Eighth Schedule. The Course will be delivered through an ODL mode of instruction. The Course will include contact programmes, school-based practicum (practice teaching, reflective journals, portfolios). video tutorial, e-learning materials, and digital platforms. This approach ensures that in-service teachers can actively engage with the course content while balancing their professional responsibilities.
